narrative.overview: LedgerFlow looks like a set of books that can be checked. Every screen is built so that a figure can be read, compared and traced back: tabular numerals, right-aligned amounts, an unambiguous sign, and a surface quiet enough that nothing competes with the numbers. It is a working tool for long sessions, so it favours density and consistency over expression. Brand shows up in precise details, not in decoration.
keyCharacteristics: Dense but scannable; text-sm is the working size.
Flat by default; structure comes from borders, not shadows.
One accent (orange); semantic colours only for status and sign.
Amounts are always monospace, tabular and right-aligned.

rules.name: The Single Accent Rule
rules.body: Orange is for the next action and the current place. It is never used for decoration, and never to signal a status; status has its own semantic hues.

rules.name: The Sign Rule
rules.body: Colour never carries a sign alone. A negative amount is red and shows its minus sign.

rules.name: The Aligned Figures Rule
rules.body: Amounts are monospace, tabular and right-aligned. No exception, including KPI cards and totals.

rules.name: The Border-First Rule
rules.body: Separate with a border before reaching for a shadow.

dos: Do right-align amounts and set them in monospace with tabular numerals.
Do use the primary-* scale (orange) for the primary action, active navigation and links.
Do separate surfaces with a 1px Hairline border before adding a shadow.
Do write all user-visible text in English.
Do keep a visible 2px orange focus ring and meet WCAG AA contrast.
Do build with the existing Ui:: ViewComponents rather than ad hoc markup.
donts: Don't use indigo or violet; the brand colour replaced them (migration still in progress).
Don't signal status with orange, or a sign with colour alone.
Don't add decorative gradients, glows or heavy shadows to working screens.
Don't use Float representations or unformatted numbers in the UI; amounts are always formatted decimals.
Don't introduce a second accent colour or a different font family.
